metadata.explanation: Chains the original title-case goal with a new objective: center-align the title paragraph. The getter downloads the docx, checks title case on all content paragraphs, and checks if para 0 alignment == WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER (int value 1). The initial document has no explicit alignment (None) so both checks fail as negative controls. After applying Capitalize Every Word + center alignment to the title, both pass for full credit (0.5 each).

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly downloads the saved docx file and parses it with python-docx, ensuring fresh state via postconfig Ctrl+S.
Title case check iterates all content paragraphs and verifies each word's first alphabetic character is uppercase, correctly matching the instruction 'capitalize the first letter of each word'.
Center alignment check uses WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER (int value 1) on para[0], correctly targeting the title paragraph.
Metric awards 0.5 per sub-goal (title_case_applied and title_centered), consistent with the dual-objective instruction and partial-credit design.
Negative control is valid: the initial document has no explicit alignment (None) so title_centered is False, and unmodified text has lowercase words so title_case_applied is False.
Error handling returns 0.0 on file-not-found or parse errors, preventing false positives.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: para[0] is assumed to be the title paragraph by index. If the document starts with an empty paragraph or the heading uses a 'Heading 1' style, consider also checking by paragraph style name as a fallback.
